prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you ate a salad at a barbecue. Respond to the committee.
response:
**MR. CHAIRMAN, MEMBERS OF THE COMMITTEE:**

I am here today under oath, and I will be direct.

I have never, at any time, in any location, consumed a salad at a barbecue. I reject the allegation in its entirety as false, malicious, and frankly un-American.

I believe in the sacred traditions of outdoor cooking: fire, smoke, meat, and perhaps a modest paper plate of baked beans if the situation calls for it. Leafy greens have no place on that altar. I have always maintained this position. I maintain it now. I will maintain it in the future.

If any so-called “witness” claims to have seen me with arugula, kale, or—God forbid—a vinaigrette anywhere near a grill, they are either mistaken, lying, or agents of a foreign power attempting to undermine the American way of life.

I am not now, nor have I ever been, a salad-eater at barbecues.

I yield to no further questions on this matter and would like a pulled pork sandwich.
